items.stem:
At universities, Mexia worked with botanists including specialists who compared her samples with existing collections. She recorded each specimen's location in a field notebook, a habit that helped later researchers verify her identifications. The California Academy of Sciences, which received many of Mexia's specimens, preserves a substantial portion of her collection. She also distributed duplicate specimens to institutions such as the University of California, Berkeley, allowing researchers in different regions to study the same plants.

Because Mexia documented habitat and elevation carefully, her specimens remain useful to scientists studying changes in plant distribution. Today, her work is recognized as an important contribution to the study of Mexican and South American flora.
